items.title: How did exchange take place before money?
items.explanation: Before money existed, people used a barter system where they exchanged goods or services directly for other goods and services. For example, if you needed an extra eraser but had an extra pencil, you could swap them with your classmate who forgot their eraser. This required finding someone willing to give exactly what you wanted in return.

items.title: Why did money come into existence?
items.explanation: Money emerged because barter was inefficient and difficult. In a barter system, people had to find someone who needed their specific item (like an ox) and was willing to give exactly what they wanted in return. This required double coincidence of wants, which was rare. Money solved these problems by providing a common standard measure of value, allowing for fair exchanges without needing to compare the exact proportion of goods.

items.title: How has money transformed into various forms over time?
items.explanation: Money evolved from physical commodities like cowrie shells, salt, and cattle to standardized items like coins (e.g., Aztec copper Tajadero) and later stone discs (Rai stones in Micronesia), feathers (Tevau in the Solomon Islands), and eventually paper notes and digital payments using mobile phones and computers.
